prompt: rgb.jpg is a horizontal strip of 5 frames, left to right in time order, sampled from the few seconds of a head-mounted (egocentric) video; the camera wearer is the viewpoint. depth.jpg, segmentation.jpg and pose.jpg are the same 5 frames rendered as a monocular depth map (brighter = nearer to the camera wearer), an instance segmentation map (coloured masks with class labels), and a body/hand skeleton map (yellow = body, magenta = hands) on black. Look at all four images. For EACH of the three maps, describe the spatial understanding that map supports, using the RGB strip for context: the layout of the scene; which people and objects are present and roughly how far each is from the camera wearer (in metres) and from each other; relative positions (left/right/in front/behind, above/below); which way people face and whether they look toward the camera wearer; what is within arm's reach of the camera wearer or of others; occlusions and anything partly out of view; and how these change across the 5 frames (approach, retreat, turning). Say what each map shows that is hard to see in the RGB alone, and where the map looks unreliable. Describe only spatial facts. Do not guess anyone's intentions, social norms, or what anyone should do. Return only JSON: {"depth": "...", "segmentation": "...", "pose": "..."} with 3-5 sentences each.

descriptions.depth: The depth map shows a sloped sandy beach scene where the camera wearer is reclining on a right-side lounge chair, holding an open book within arm's reach at roughly 0.3 to 0.5 metres (brightest white) that partially occludes their mid-legs, while their torso is below the book (~0.2–0.4 m) and crossed feet extend forward to about 1.2 to 1.5 metres. To the left, about 1.2 to 2.0 metres from the camera wearer and 1.0 metre from the wearer's chair, a second person reclines on another lounge chair facing upward and forward toward the water (not looking at the camera wearer), with their head and upper torso partly out of view at the left frame edge, except in frame 4 where a slight leftward camera pan brings their head briefly into view; between the two chairs stands a wooden umbrella pole (~1.5–1.8 m away) with an elevated shelf holding clothing and bottles above the chairs. Across the five frames, the scene layout and relative distances remain nearly static with no approach or retreat, apart from minor head-rotation shifts in frame 4. Compared to RGB alone, the depth map clearly separates the foreground book, mid-ground umbrella post, and continuous receding ground plane of the beach out to the distant hut (>10 m, dark grey), though it is unreliable on the second person on the left lounge chair, merging their legs and body seamlessly into the chair's depth profile, and assigns an artificially black infinite depth to the distant sky and ocean horizon.
descriptions.segmentation: The instance segmentation map identifies discrete masks in the foreground, separating the open `book` (0.3–0.5 metres away, within the camera wearer's grasp) from the camera wearer's own arms, torso, and extended legs (`person`, spanning ~0.2 to 1.5 metres in front and below the book, which occludes the wearer's knees). To the left at roughly 1.2 to 2.0 metres away, it segments the reclining companion (`person`) who faces forward toward the shoreline away from the camera wearer and has their upper body cut off by the left frame border, as well as the supporting lounge `chair` beneath them (~1.2–2.2 m away). Across the five frames, the spatial positions of the wearer and companion stay stationary, with only small mask shifts as the camera tilts slightly left in frame 4 and back in frame 5. While segmentation makes the exact boundary between the held book and the wearer's occluding thumbs and hands clearer than in the low-contrast shadow of the RGB image, it is highly unreliable elsewhere: in frames 1 through 4 it falsely labels the dark clothing and bottles resting high on the umbrella pole shelf (~1.5 m away, above and left of the wearer) as a `person`, in frames 2 and 3 it bleeds the `book` mask onto the wearer's lower legs or lounge chair stripes, and in frame 5 it completely misses the reclining person on the left while only labeling their `chair`.
descriptions.pose: The pose map is almost entirely blank across the five-frame sequence, detecting only a single magenta hand skeleton for the camera wearer's left hand in frame 1 at the bottom-left of the book (~0.3–0.4 metres from the viewpoint, within immediate reach). In the RGB context, the camera wearer's two hands hold the bottom corners of the open book in front of their torso across all five frames while their legs extend forward (~1.2–1.5 m), and a second person reclines on a lounge chair 1.2 to 2.0 metres to the left facing forward toward the water with their upper body mostly out of view off the left edge. Neither person approaches, retreats, or turns toward the camera wearer over time, with only a slight leftward camera pan occurring in frame 4. In frame 1, the pose map explicitly localizes the articulated finger joints and thumb posture of the wearer's left hand gripping the page edge, which is partially shadowed in RGB. However, the map is severely unreliable overall, failing to detect the camera wearer's left hand in frames 2 through 5, missing the wearer's right hand and lower body across all frames due to self-occlusion by the book and egocentric truncation, and completely missing the reclining person on the left whose head and shoulders lie mostly outside the field of view.
